# Wispr Flow — Style Reference

> Cream stationery, a fountain-pen headline, and one lavender ticket. EB Garamond set at 400 with italic turns, a #ffffeb paper canvas, 2px ink outlines instead of shadows, and a pale lavender button as the only call.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Wispr Flow speaks a warm-stationery literary language. The canvas is a cream #ffffeb page (16 background uses). It steps down to a sand #e4e4d0 secondary surface and is broken by two full-bleed stages, forest #034f46 and ink #1a1a1a, whose 80px top corners make each band rise like a sheet of card stock. The chromatic budget is two system hues. Pale lavender #f0d7ff fills every primary action, forest #034f46 owns the announcement bar and the speed section, and coral #ff6c4c and orange #ffa946 stay inside illustration. Typography carries the thesis. EB Garamond at weight 400 only, tracked to -0.03em with a 0.95 line height, sets every headline from 32px to 120px and pivots into italic mid-sentence. Figtree at 500 and 600 handles all UI at a 1.3 line height. Elevation is drawn rather than cast: 2px #1a1a1a outlines, 1px #d1d1c1 hairlines, and exactly one 3px shadow on the entire page. The result reads as a literary magazine about speaking rather than a SaaS dashboard about AI.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cream Canvas | `#ffffeb` | `--color-cream-canvas` | Page body, nav container fill, small feature cards and reversed text on dark bands (40 text uses) — a yellow-cast paper that warms every neutral placed on it. |
| Sand Surface | `#e4e4d0` | `--color-sand-surface` | Product toggle track, language feature tile and secondary pill fills (11 uses) — one tonal step down from canvas, so depth comes from tone without any shadow. |
| Forest Stage | `#034f46` | `--color-forest-stage` | Announcement bar, the "4x faster" speed section and its stat-card backdrop — a full-bleed inverted stage. Do not promote it to button fills. |
| Ink | `#1a1a1a` | `--color-ink` | All headlines, body copy, CTA borders, the logo marquee band and the transcript ribbon (185 text uses) — a softened black that keeps contrast high without the glare of pure black. |
| Ink Caption | `#1a1a1ab3` | `--color-ink-caption` | Nav links, eyebrow labels and privacy-section paragraphs (12 uses) — ink at 70% alpha, so secondary text inherits the cream warmth underneath. |
| Ink Whisper | `#1a1a1a80` | `--color-ink-whisper` | Availability caption, the arcing raw-speech text in the hero and ghosted transcript fragments (11 uses) — ink at 50% alpha for tertiary content. Never set body copy in it. |
| Stone Border | `#d1d1c1` | `--color-stone-border` | 1px ring around the floating nav container and card dividers (6 uses) — a warm hairline that frames without lifting. |
| Linen Ring | `#eeebe3` | `--color-linen-ring` | 2px ring on the dark waveform badge and 1px rules on light tiles — a near-canvas line that separates ink objects from photography. |
| Lavender Signal | `#f0d7ff` | `--color-lavender-signal` | Every "Download for free" button fill (5 uses) — the single action color, pastel enough to sit on cream without shouting. Do not use it for decoration. |
| Ember Coral | `#ff6c4c` | `--color-ember-coral` | Illustration accents, mockup highlights and inline link moments (3 uses) — decorative heat. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Sunbeam Orange | `#ffa946` | `--color-sunbeam-orange` | Feature illustrations and mockup chips (4 uses) — a decorative companion to coral, permitted only inside drawn or mocked content. |
| Mint Pulse | `#34d399` | `--color-mint-pulse` | Live or recording status dot in product mockups (1 use) — status-only green, sized as a dot and never as a fill. |

## Tokens — Typography

### EB Garamond — the display voice: every headline, stat and pull-quote, always weight 400 · `--font-eb-garamond`

- **Substitute:** EB Garamond at 400 (the same open-source face, free on Google Fonts), Cormorant Garamond at 500 (Cormorant draws thinner than its number, so step up one weight to match stroke), Crimson Pro at 400.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 20px, 26px, 32px, 48px, 64px, 75px, 96px, 120px
- **Line height:** 0.85 (120px), 0.95 (20–96px), 1.0 (75px)
- **Letter spacing:** -0.96px at 32px, -1.44px at 48px, -1.92px at 64px, -2.25px at 75px, -2.88px at 96px, -3.6px at 120px (a constant -0.03em), normal at 20px and 26px
- **Role:** A Renaissance book face at weight 400 on a productivity tool is the signature. Headlines are massive and quiet, and hierarchy comes from size and the roman-to-italic pivot rather than weight. The scale jumps by roughly a Perfect Fifth (32 → 48 → 64 → 96 is 1.5 / 1.33 / 1.5), which is far steeper than the conventional Major Third 1.25. Combined with sub-1.0 leading, each heading becomes a typeset object rather than a label. The constant -0.03em tracking pulls Garamond's generous book spacing into display tightness.

### Figtree — the UI and body workhorse, geometric and friendly at medium weights · `--font-figtree`

- **Substitute:** Figtree at 500 (free on Google Fonts), DM Sans at 500, Outfit at 500 (Outfit renders slightly lighter, so use 600 where Figtree uses 600 or above). Figtree's 500 reads as a true medium, so do not drop substitutes to 400.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 11px, 12px, 13px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 36px
- **Line height:** 1.0 (buttons and nav at 16px), 1.3 (default), 1.33 (15px), 1.54 (12px)
- **Letter spacing:** 1.12px at 14px uppercase eyebrows (0.08em), -0.24px at 12px, normal elsewhere
- **Role:** Weight 500 is the workhorse (93 uses against 6 at 400). This is anti-convention: most marketing sites set body at 400, and the extra stroke here lets sans copy hold its own beside a large serif. Weight 600 runs every interactive label and 700 is rationed to 11px mockup chrome. The pairing is literary serif for meaning and geometric sans for mechanism, and the flat 1.3 leading keeps UI blocks compact under airy headlines.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Figtree | 700 | 11px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Figtree | 500 | 13px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Figtree | 500 | 14px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Figtree | 500 | 16px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Figtree | 500 | 20px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | EB Garamond | 400 | 32px | 0.95 | -0.96px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | EB Garamond | 400 | 48px | 0.95 | -1.44px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | EB Garamond | 400 | 64px | 0.95 | -1.92px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | EB Garamond | 400 | 75px | 1.0 | -2.25px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | EB Garamond | 400 | 96px | 0.95 | -2.88px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in EB Garamond at weight 400 with -0.03em tracking (-2.88px at 96px, -1.92px at 64px) — size alone carries hierarchy, which is what makes the serif read as authorship rather than marketing.
- Turn the second clause of a headline into italic at the same 400 weight ("just speak.", "than typing") — the italic is a change of voice, giving emphasis without a single bold stroke.
- Fill primary actions with #f0d7ff, a 2px #1a1a1a border, 8px radius and 16px 24px padding — the drawn outline replaces the shadow and keeps the button legible as the only colored object in view.
- Keep the page on #ffffeb rather than pure white and step down to #e4e4d0 for secondary surfaces — the yellow cast is what makes #1a1a1a ink and lavender read as stationery.
- Set UI copy in Figtree weight 500 at 16px with 1.3 line height (20.8px), and labels in weight 600 — the heavier sans holds its ground next to 96px serif headlines.
- Open each dark band (#1a1a1a or #034f46) with 80px 80px 0px 0px corners and 64px to 128px internal padding — sections overlap like stacked card stock instead of abutting.
- Separate surfaces with a 1px #d1d1c1 hairline or a tone shift — never with layered drop shadows, because the page has exactly one shadow token and it stays at 1px 1px 3px.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 at 48px and above — the whole system rests on weight 400 restraint, and a heavy Garamond turns the literary register into a sales banner.
- Don't make #ff6c4c the button or link color just because it is the brightest hue — coral is illustration-only, and promoting it would split the action budget away from #f0d7ff.
- Don't give the primary button the 1600px pill radius — the pill belongs to the sand product toggle, and the 8px corner is what distinguishes committing from switching.
- Don't loosen display leading to Figtree's 1.3 — EB Garamond at 0.95 is what makes headlines stack into tight typeset blocks, and open leading breaks them into loose lines.
- Don't add a heavier shadow than `--shadow-subtle` to cards or the nav — elevation is drawn with 2px #1a1a1a and 1px #d1d1c1 lines, and cast shadows muddy the cream paper.
- Don't set body paragraphs in Figtree 400 at 16px — 500 is the workhorse (93 uses), and the lighter weight goes spindly beside the serif.
- Don't push secondary text below #1a1a1a80 or swap the alpha inks for opaque grays — the 70% and 50% inks inherit canvas warmth, and opaque grays read cold against #ffffeb. Tinted-ink secondary text is non-negotiable.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffeb (Cream Canvas)
- secondary surface: #e4e4d0 (Sand Surface)
- inverted stage: #034f46 (Forest Stage)
- primary text: #1a1a1a (Ink)
- secondary text: #1a1a1ab3 (Ink Caption)
- hairline: #d1d1c1 (Stone Border)
- primary action: #f0d7ff (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts stay neutral: use #1a1a1a and #e4e4d0 for comparison series, #034f46 as the solid fill for the single Flow series, and #f0d7ff only to highlight one bar, so no decorative coral or orange ever becomes the loudest mark on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor reading "Download for free" with background #f0d7ff, text color #1a1a1a, border 2px solid #1a1a1a, border-radius 8px, padding 16px 24px, height 52px, font Figtree 16px weight 600 with line-height 1.0 and normal letter-spacing, and no box-shadow. On hover, switch the background to #e4e4d0 while keeping the 2px #1a1a1a border, with a 150ms transition. Do not round it to a pill.

2. Build a hero section on #ffffeb, centered, with 128px top padding. Add an eyebrow "WISPR FLOW DICTATION" in Figtree 14px weight 500, uppercase, letter-spacing 1.12px, color #1a1a1ab3, and 24px below it. Follow with an h1 in EB Garamond 96px weight 400, line-height 0.95, letter-spacing -2.88px, color #1a1a1a, max-width 992px. Line one is roman "Don't type," and line two is italic "just speak." at the same weight. Add a lede in Figtree 20px weight 500, line-height 1.3, color #1a1a1a, max-width 480px, 24px below the h1. Then add the primary button 32px below, and a caption "Available on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android" in Figtree 13px weight 500, color #1a1a1a80, 16px below the button.

3. Build a navigation bar: a 912px-wide centered container, 52px tall, background #ffffeb, border 1px solid #d1d1c1, border-radius 8px, padding 0 8px 0 16px, not sticky, 32px below the page top. On the left, place a wordmark followed by a segmented toggle: track #e4e4d0, radius 1600px, padding 4px. The active segment is #ffffeb with radius 1600px and padding 8px 12px, and labels are Figtree 14px weight 500 #1a1a1a. On the right, place links "Business", "Pricing" and "Lab" in Figtree 16px weight 600, line-height 1.0, color #1a1a1ab3, gap 24px, then the primary lavender button.

4. Build a comparison stat section on a full-bleed #034f46 band with border-radius 80px 80px 0px 0px and 128px vertical padding. Center a headline in EB Garamond 96px weight 400, letter-spacing -2.88px, color #ffffeb, reading "4x faster" in roman and "than typing" in italic, with a Figtree 20px weight 500 #ffffeb lede at 768px max-width, 24px below. Below it, create a 1:3 row with a 16px gap. The left card is transparent with a 2px #ffffeb border at 10% alpha, radius 32px and 16px padding, showing "Keyboard" in Figtree 16px weight 500 and "45 wpm" in EB Garamond 48px weight 400 with -1.44px tracking. The right card is a motion-blurred photo with radius 32px showing "Flow" and "220 wpm" in the same type in #ffffeb, with no shadows.

5. Build a testimonial card with no background, border-radius 48px and padding 16px. Set the quote in EB Garamond 32px weight 400, line-height 0.95, letter-spacing -0.96px, color #1a1a1a, max-width 506px. Below it, after a 16px gap, add a row with a 48px avatar at 50% radius and attribution in Figtree 14px weight 500, color #1a1a1ab3. No border, no shadow.

### Navigation Bar — Floating Framed

**Role:** Primary wayfinding in bordered capsule

### Segmented Pill — Sand (Secondary)

**Role:** Product switch, secondary action

Soft and tonal. The track is #e4e4d0 with 1600px radius and 4px internal padding. The active segment is #ffffeb with 1600px radius and padding 8px 12px, and the inactive label sits directly on sand. Text is #1a1a1a in Figtree 14px weight 500, with no border and no shadow. This is the deliberate shape outlier: the full pill is reserved for switching contexts (Dictation/Notetaker), while committing actions keep the 8px corner.

### Eyebrow Label

**Role:** Section kicker above serif headlines

Uppercase, tracked and small. No background, color #1a1a1ab3 on cream or #ffffeb on dark bands, Figtree 14px weight 500, line height 1.3, letter-spacing 1.12px (0.08em), uppercase, with 24px below before the headline. ### Hero Headline — Roman to Italic Pivot

**Role:** The thesis in one sentence

A two-line literary sentence. EB Garamond 96px weight 400, line height 0.95, letter-spacing -2.88px, color #1a1a1a, centered within 992px. Line one is roman ("Don't type,") and line two is italic at the same weight ("just speak."). A Figtree 20px weight 500 lede at line height 1.3 and 480px max-width sits 24px below. The italic turn substitutes for the bold keyword a conventional SaaS hero would use: emphasis through voice, not weight.

### Dictation Waveform Pill

**Role:** Product glyph and listening state

The product's own icon as a component. The large hero version is a #ffffeb pill with a 2px #1a1a1a border, 1600px radius and a centered #1a1a1a bar waveform. The compact version is #1a1a1a with a 2px #eeebe3 ring, 52px radius, 6px padding and a 56 × 30px footprint, placed over photography with no shadow. It reproduces the Flow desktop widget literally, so the interface on the page is the interface on your screen.

### Transcript Ribbon Illustration

**Role:** Messy speech becomes polished text

The hero's narrative device. Raw speech arcs across the cream canvas in Figtree 20px weight 500, color #1a1a1a80, looping through the waveform pill. It exits as a #1a1a1a ribbon band carrying #ffffeb text in Figtree 20px weight 600, about 40px tall (estimated), rotated and curving off-canvas. There is no border radius on the band and no shadow. Use the grey-in, ink-out contrast whenever the product transformation needs to be shown rather than told.

### Logo Marquee Band — Ink Sheet

**Role:** Social proof on inverted stage

An ink sheet rising from the page. Background #1a1a1a, radius 80px 80px 0px 0px, eyebrow in Figtree 14px weight 500 uppercase with 1.12px tracking in #ffffeb, and logos rendered monochrome #ffffeb at 19 to 31px height spaced 64px apart, scrolling horizontally. The section has 64px vertical padding and no shadow. The rounded top edge turns a section change into a physical overlap, unlike the conventional straight-edged logo strip.

### Comparison Stat Card — Keyboard vs Flow

**Role:** The 4x speed proof

Main content card on the forest stage. The keyboard card is transparent over #034f46 with a 2px #ffffeb ring at reduced opacity (decorative alpha, not a system token) and a 32px radius. The Flow card is full-bleed motion-blurred photography at a 32px radius. Labels are Figtree 16px weight 500 #ffffeb, and stats ("220 wpm") are EB Garamond 48px weight 400, -1.44px, with 16px padding and no shadow. Narrow-versus-wide proportion makes the argument visually.

### Feature Tile — Sand and Cream

**Role:** Individual capability demonstration

Small, flat, tonal. The cream variant uses #ffffeb with a 16px radius and 16px padding, and the sand variant uses #e4e4d0 with a 16px radius and padding 56px 0px 0px so its mockup bleeds to the bottom edge. Body copy is #1a1a1a in Figtree 16px weight 400 or 500, mockup chips use Figtree 11px weight 700 with 4px radius, and there is no border and no shadow. Tone shift alone separates tile from page, a stricter rule than the conventional card shadow.

### Testimonial Card — Pull Quote

**Role:** Customer voice as editorial quote

Magazine pull-quote rather than review widget. It has no fill, a 48px radius and 16px padding. The quote is EB Garamond 32px weight 400, line height 0.95, -0.96px tracking, color #1a1a1a, at 506px measure. Attribution ("Host of Diary of a CEO") is Figtree 14px weight 500 in #1a1a1ab3, with a 50%-radius avatar and no shadow. The 48px radius is the largest card corner in the system, saved for human voices.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline in EB Garamond at weight 400 with -0.03em tracking (-2.88px at 96px, -1.92px at 64px) — size alone carries hierarchy, which is what makes the serif read as authorship rather than marketing.
- Turn the second clause of a headline into italic at the same 400 weight ("just speak.", "than typing") — the italic is a change of voice, giving emphasis without a single bold stroke.
- Fill primary actions with #f0d7ff, a 2px #1a1a1a border, 8px radius and 16px 24px padding — the drawn outline replaces the shadow and keeps the button legible as the only colored object in view.
- Keep the page on #ffffeb rather than pure white and step down to #e4e4d0 for secondary surfaces — the yellow cast is what makes #1a1a1a ink and lavender read as stationery.
- Set UI copy in Figtree weight 500 at 16px with 1.3 line height (20.8px), and labels in weight 600 — the heavier sans holds its ground next to 96px serif headlines.
- Open each dark band (#1a1a1a or #034f46) with 80px 80px 0px 0px corners and 64px to 128px internal padding — sections overlap like stacked card stock instead of abutting.
- Separate surfaces with a 1px #d1d1c1 hairline or a tone shift — never with layered drop shadows, because the page has exactly one shadow token and it stays at 1px 1px 3px.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 at 48px and above — the whole system rests on weight 400 restraint, and a heavy Garamond turns the literary register into a sales banner.
- Don't make #ff6c4c the button or link color just because it is the brightest hue — coral is illustration-only, and promoting it would split the action budget away from #f0d7ff.
- Don't give the primary button the 1600px pill radius — the pill belongs to the sand product toggle, and the 8px corner is what distinguishes committing from switching.
- Don't loosen display leading to Figtree's 1.3 — EB Garamond at 0.95 is what makes headlines stack into tight typeset blocks, and open leading breaks them into loose lines.
- Don't add a heavier shadow than `--shadow-subtle` to cards or the nav — elevation is drawn with 2px #1a1a1a and 1px #d1d1c1 lines, and cast shadows muddy the cream paper.
- Don't set body paragraphs in Figtree 400 at 16px — 500 is the workhorse (93 uses), and the lighter weight goes spindly beside the serif.
- Don't push secondary text below #1a1a1a80 or swap the alpha inks for opaque grays — the 70% and 50% inks inherit canvas warmth, and opaque grays read cold against #ffffeb. Tinted-ink secondary text is non-negotiable.

## Surfaces

| Level | Name | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Cream Canvas | `#ffffeb` | Page body, hero, nav container and cream feature tiles |
| 1 | Sand Surface | `#e4e4d0` | Toggle track, secondary pills and sand feature tiles one tonal step down |
| 2 | Forest Stage | `#034f46` | Announcement bar and the full-bleed speed section with comparison cards |
| 3 | Ink | `#1a1a1a` | Logo marquee sheet, transcript ribbon and compact waveform badge as the fully inverted layer |

## Elevation

- **Rare floating chip in mockups (the single measured shadow):** `1px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`

Everything else is flat. Depth comes from three substitutes: a 2px #1a1a1a outline on actions and the waveform pill, a 1px #d1d1c1 hairline on the nav capsule, and tonal steps from #ffffeb to #e4e4d0 to #034f46 to #1a1a1a. Sections rise through 80px top-corner overlaps rather than shadow, so the UI feels like printed paper layered on a desk rather than glass floating over a screen.

## Imagery

Imagery splits into three registers. The first is full-bleed lifestyle photography rendered with heavy motion blur: a figure by a window, warm amber and sky blue. It sits inside 32px-radius cards on the forest stage with no border and no shadow, conveying speed as a physical sensation. The second is product mockups built from live HTML, not screenshots: vocabulary panels, language tiles and filler-word cleanup chips, set on 16px tiles with Figtree 11px weight 700 chips at 4px radius. The third is typographic illustration, where curving transcript text and the waveform glyph act as the hero image itself. Coral #ff6c4c, orange #ffa946 and a decorative pink #ffbcf2 (decorative, not a system token) appear only inside these illustrations. There are no gradients, orbs or glows, and icons are monochrome #1a1a1a line glyphs. The narrative is your rambling voice becoming finished prose.

## Layout

Content centers in a 1240px max-width, with the nav capsule narrower at 912px and headline measures held to 768px to 992px. Sections breathe at 128px rhythm (64px to 160px). The hero is fully centered: eyebrow, two-line 96px serif headline, a 480px lede, one lavender CTA, a 13px availability caption, then the transcript-ribbon illustration filling the lower fold. Sections alternate cream → ink logo sheet → forest speed stage → cream features, with each dark band opening on 80px top corners. Features use 2- and 3-column tile grids, the logo row is a 9-item horizontal marquee, and the comparison is a 1:3 asymmetric pair. The nav is non-sticky at 52px, with logo and toggle left and links plus CTA right. The footer is a full-width multi-column directory under uppercase headings with 48px bottom padding. At 375px, set display headlines at 48px and section gaps at 64px. Density: spacious.

**Example Component Prompts**

Build a Primary Action Button: an anchor reading "Download for free" with background #f0d7ff, text color #1a1a1a, border 2px solid #1a1a1a, border-radius 8px, padding 16px 24px, height 52px, font Figtree 16px weight 600 with line-height 1.0 and normal letter-spacing, and no box-shadow. Below it, create a 1:3 row with a 16px gap. ## Literary Headlines

The discipline is a single serif at a single weight. EB Garamond sets every headline, stat and quote at 400, and hierarchy moves only through size (32 → 48 → 64 → 96px), a constant -0.03em tracking and the roman-to-italic pivot. Three moves would break it: adding a second display face, bolding any Garamond line, or replacing the italic turn with a colored keyword. Each turns literature back into advertising. To extend the system, take new heading sizes from the existing steps and keep leading at 0.95. Put emphasis in italic and push functional detail (prices, counts, labels) down into Figtree 500 or 600. A pricing page should still set its plan names in Garamond 48px roman with italic qualifiers.

## Drawn Not Cast

Elevation in this system is line work. The lavender button owns a 2px #1a1a1a border, the nav capsule a 1px #d1d1c1 ring, and the waveform badge a 2px #eeebe3 ring, while the page carries exactly one 1px 1px 3px shadow. It breaks the moment a designer reaches for conventional card shadows, glassmorphism or blurred glows, because the cream paper then reads as a screen. To extend it, give new interactive objects a 2px #1a1a1a outline, give new containers a 1px #d1d1c1 hairline or a tone step to #e4e4d0, and signal layering through 80px section corners rather than z-depth.

## Rationed Color

The color budget is two system hues with strict jobs. Lavender #f0d7ff means "act", and forest #034f46 means "stage". Coral #ff6c4c and orange #ffa946 live only inside illustrations and mockups, and mint #34d399 is a status dot. The rationing breaks if lavender appears on badges or backgrounds, if coral becomes a link color, or if a third stage hue joins the alternation of cream, ink and forest. New features should borrow forest for one hero band at most, keep every other surface on #ffffeb or #e4e4d0, and route any new accent into illustration where it cannot compete with the button.

## Similar Brands

- **Anthropic** — shares the warm off-white canvas with weight-400 serif display headlines and near-black ink, but uses terracotta where Wispr Flow uses a pale lavender action.
- **Mailchimp** — shares the editorial serif headline on a warm canvas with ink-outlined illustration, though Mailchimp spends far more of its color budget on saturated yellow.
- **Granola** — a category competitor in AI note-taking with a warm, paper-like neutral canvas and understated chrome, without Wispr Flow's roman-to-italic Garamond signature.
- **Otter.ai** — a direct voice-transcription competitor whose blue-on-white SaaS conventions make it the useful contrast case for Wispr Flow's literary cream system.
- **Arc (The Browser Company)** — shares the playful, physical section transitions and oversized type, but leans on gradients where Wispr Flow stays strictly flat.
